alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive form takes the ASV's And under rule 14.
Preposition with its own English word.
Demonstrative object of the preposition.
Explicit subject noun takes only its own English; the ASV fronts it before the verb.
Finite verb; the explicit subject stands separately, so the verb keeps only the lexical predicate.
Hebrew has no indefinite article, so the supplied a belongs to the numeral that licenses it under rule 15; headed on the word carrying the lexeme.
The single waw of the numeral phrase stands between the same two numerals the English and joins (rule 42).
Tens numeral.
Counted noun; only one occurrence is written, so no rule 22 distribution arises.

Waw of the second consecutive verb takes the written and. Variant WLC.JOB.42.16.v004 is underdetermined and its base reading is retained; both readings write this waw and verb, so nothing in the alignment turns on it.
Finite verb, subject continued from the preceding clause and not separately written in English.
Object marker with no English of its own; the ASV writes the object bare (rule 16).
Pronominal suffix rendered by the possessive his (rule 18).
Host noun keeps its own word.
Coordinating waw.
Second object marker, likewise unrendered.
Suffix on the nomen rectum takes the possessive his standing at the phrase's left edge, since an English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor (rule 29's possessive reading).
Nomen rectum sons, written as the English possessive before its head noun.
Construct noun; the relation is carried by the English possessive rather than by an of, so this noun keeps only its own word (rule 19).

Appositional even before four generations: the verse's two object markers stand on the sons phrases, which the ASV renders bare, and no marker stands on this appositive, so no morpheme licenses the word (rule 16). The ASV italic corroborates without deciding it (rule 7).
Numeral.
Counted noun of the appositive phrase.

review_notes: Alternative considered for t019 even: attaching it to one of the object markers as an appositional even under rule 16. Rejected because neither marker stands on the appositive phrase the word introduces, and rule 16 forbids reaching across the clause for a marker to carry it.

The possessive run his sons sons was read as rule 29's possessive shape: the determiner-position his belongs to the suffix on the rectum, the first written sons to the rectum בָנָיו, and the second to the construct בְּנֵי. The competing linear reading would give t017 to the construct and t018 to the rectum, but the English possessive precedes its head noun.
Variant WLC.JOB.42.16.v004 is marked underdetermined with the base reading retained; it is not a rule 53 exclusion and no English is affected.
